# comment: AI-READI clinical_data/observation.csv items mapped to HPO. EVERY ROW IS SELF-REPORT (evidence_code ECO:0006160), so the questionnaire rules apply unchanged - only exactMatch and broadMatch rows gate, every gate is bounded (in {..} or >=n & <=m, never an open >=, so a refusal code 555/777/888/999 cannot fire it), and ONLY PRESENCE is asserted, because a low answer denies the symptom within the instrument's recall window and not the phenotype (docs/mapping-conventions.md, Why absence is not asserted). Subjects are b2ai:observation.<redcap_variable>; the OMOP table qualifier matters - the same variables in condition_occurrence are asserted conditions, mapped to MONDO in b2ai-aireadi-conditions. Answer values are the stored value_as_number; ces5 and ces8 are stored already reverse-scored (3 = rarely) so higher always means more distress. GATED ROWS - the CES-D-10 items and total, which config/aireadi/observation/cesd10.yaml ingests. Cut-points follow the repo rule of comparing answer LABELS, not integers - CES-D's '1-2 days of the past week' is the endorsement PHQ-9 gates at 'Several days' - and are marked pending the same clinical review the Voice set had; an earlier adversarial review disputed direction and cut-point on several proposed CES-D rows, and each row records its reasoning so a reviewer can rule on it. UNGATED ROWS, deliberately - the medical-history grid (mhoccur_*, mhterm_*, mh_*), falls, and the vision-function items are mapped term-to-term with the intended gate written in the comment, but carry no when_value because scope.yaml does not ingest them and a gated row must name an emitted assay (tests/test_config_mappings.py). Landing those gates is a config change plus filling the column, nothing else. NOT MAPPED, and why - ces9 'I felt lonely' (no HPO term for loneliness); PAID-5 (distress about living with diabetes is a disease-specific appraisal, not a phenotype - see paid5.yaml); mhoccur_ms (a disease with no HPO phenotype term; MONDO only); diet, substance-use, self-management, family-history, medication, social-determinant, imaging-flag and administrative families (not phenotypes of the participant).
